Package bakerydms

Class OrderManager

  • java.lang.Object
    • bakerydms.OrderManager
  • public class OrderManager
extends java.lang.Object
    Carries out every action on orders (the business logic layer).

    The window calls this class for each CRUD operation and for the custom action. OrderManager:

    • checks every value with OrderValidator before anything is stored,
    • stores and reads orders through an OrderRepository (the MySQL database in the real program, or an in-memory copy in the unit tests),
    • calculates order totals with tax, and
    • builds the DailyReport for the Daily Production Report.
    Methods that change data return a list of problems; an empty list means the change was saved. Until connectTo(OrderRepository) is called, data methods throw a DataAccessException saying no database is connected.

    Usage: 

    
 OrderManager manager = new OrderManager(new OrderValidator(cakeTypes), 0.07);
 manager.connectTo(connector.connect("localhost", "3306", "bakery_dms", "root", password));
 List<String> problems = manager.addOrder(1026, "Dana Lee", "4075559876", "Red Velvet",
         2, 28.00, LocalDate.of(2027, 2, 13), "Write Happy Birthday, Dana!");
 DailyReport report = manager.generateDailyReport(LocalDate.of(2027, 2, 13));
    Version:
    4.0 (Phase 4, Module 11)
    Author:
    Kayla Ewing
    See Also:
    OrderRepository, BakeryOrderWindow

        specialInstructions - notes for the baker (may be empty)

        Throws:

      • updateField

        public java.util.List<java.lang.String> updateField​(int orderId,
                                                    int fieldNumber,
                                                    java.lang.String newValue)
        Changes ONE field of an order using exactly what the user typed. The text is converted to the right data type here, then the whole order is checked by updateOrder(int, Order) before anything is saved, so a bad value never changes the stored order. The unit tests use this method to prove every one of the nine fields can be updated.

        Field numbers:

        1. Order ID
        2. Customer name
        3. Phone number
        4. Cake type
        5. Quantity
        6. Unit price
        7. Pickup date
        8. Picked up (yes/no)
        9. Special instructions
        Parameters:
        orderId - the ID of the order to change
        fieldNumber - which field to change (1-9)
        newValue - the new value exactly as the user typed it
        Returns:
        a list of problems; an EMPTY list means the field was updated
        Throws:
        DataAccessException - if no database is connected yet, or the database cannot be reached

      • generateDailyReport

        public DailyReport generateDailyReport​(java.time.LocalDate date)
        CUSTOM ACTION: Daily Production Report. For the chosen pickup date, counts how many cakes of each type must be baked and calculates the expected revenue. Only orders that are due on that date AND have not been picked up yet are counted; the database query selects exactly those orders, and the totals are calculated here.
        Parameters:
        date - the pickup date to report on
        Returns:
        the finished report (with zero orders if nothing is due)
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - if the date is null
        DataAccessException - if no database is connected yet, or the database cannot be reached
